title: Capture a real operator price twice per game week
problem: Every certification gate that depends on price fails, not because the signals are bad but because no verified opening or closing price exists anywhere in the repo.
option_a: Do nothing; keep the board permanently in paper and say so.
option_b: Capture one operator's NFL page on a fixed schedule (Tuesday and three hours before kickoff), store the raw snapshot with a UTC stamp, and populate MARKET_OPEN and MARKET_CLOSE from it.
option_c: Buy or licence a commercial odds history and ingest it.
evidence: price-store.html - 156 of 390 snapshot rows are empty, all for want of a publisher
review_test: If two consecutive weeks of captures produce an opening and a closing price for at least 90% of originated markets, this becomes the default and G2 becomes testable.

title: Rebuild the totals model before trusting any total or moneyline
problem: The totals model's out-of-sample MAE is statistically indistinguishable from always predicting the league average, yet the moneyline is derived from the side and the total together.
option_a: Keep the current model and publish the total with a health warning.
option_b: Rebuild it on pace and efficiency inputs, re-measure against the same naive baseline, and only then re-derive the moneyline.
option_c: Stop originating totals and price only the side and the moneyline.
review_test: If the rebuilt model does not beat the naive baseline by at least 0.5 points of MAE on a held-out season, take option C.

title: Grade parlays against an empirical joint, never independent legs
problem: The two-leg parlay family prices its legs independently. The board shows it needs 27.44% to break even and delivered 26.32% over 1,953 bets, so the independence assumption is doing real work.
option_a: Keep independent pricing and accept the error.
option_b: Require an empirical joint estimate for every leg pair, and refuse the bet when the market price assumes independence and we cannot measure the joint.
option_c: Drop parlays from the board until the joint can be measured.
evidence: strategies.html - S8 on the research board
review_test: If the joint cannot be estimated for a leg pair within one season, that pair is refused automatically.

title: Put a confidence interval on every published model coefficient
problem: Home-field advantage is published as a point estimate with no interval, and a reader cannot tell it apart from zero.
option_a: Leave point estimates as they are.
option_b: Publish a bootstrap interval beside every coefficient, including home-field advantage and each team rating.
option_c: Publish intervals and suppress any coefficient whose interval contains zero from the headline tables.
evidence: lines.html - home-field advantage fitted at +0.21 pts
review_test: If an interval cannot be computed for a coefficient, that coefficient is published blank rather than as a bare number.

title: Fix the multiplicity budget before more families are tried
problem: Nine families were pre-registered for one build; the Holm correction is only honest if the family count is fixed in advance.
option_a: Keep adding families and accept the looser correction.
option_b: Agree a per-season family budget and pre-register it; the correction uses that budget.
option_c: Pre-register the budget and make it a hard cap on certification.
review_test: If the owner will not fix a budget, record the unbounded-multiplicity caveat on every leaderboard.

title: Extend the official results feed backwards before certifying anything
problem: The certification universe gives each family 4-51 graded bets against a 300 minimum; the fix is more official history, not a lower bar.
option_a: Lower G1 and record the risk.
option_b: Transcribe prior-season official finals into the results feed until every family clears 300 graded bets.
option_c: Certify on the current 4-51 bet samples and say so.
review_test: If a season of transcription still leaves a family under 300, lower G1 explicitly and log the false-discovery risk.

title: Make the demotion gate automatic and dated
problem: Six triggers are defined but enforcement is manual; a gate that waits for a meeting is not a gate.
option_b: Wire D1a-D1f into the build so a trigger fires automatically and stamps the demotion date on the record.
option_c: Add a scheduled job that evaluates the triggers nightly.
review_test: If a trigger fires on the research board, the family is demoted on the certification board the same run.

title: Publish a per-team net-injury decision row
problem: Depth is captured by team but the team-level decision view does not exist as a single row per team.
option_b: Add one row per team with starters out, named replacements and a net injury count, linked to the depth source.
option_c: Add a separate team-view page only.
review_test: If the net count cannot be computed from official depth + injury rows, the row is published blank and flagged.
